content: Rifampin reduces the absorption of gastrointestinal (GI) agents, but this applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of clomipramine by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of clonazepam by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Rifampin increases the levels or effects of clopidogrel by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction may enhance the metabolism of clopidogrel to its active metabolite, potentially increasing antiplatelet effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug, and monitor patients closely for increased antiplatelet effects. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of clorazepate by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Clotrimazole increases the levels or effects of rifampin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Concomitant use of cotrimoxazole with rifampin increases rifampin concentrations, which may elevate the risk of toxicity. Monitor for adverse reactions during coadministration. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of clozapine by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as this interaction is considered serious. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated due to the potential for loss of therapeutic effect and the development of resistance. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of cobimetinib by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration, as strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers may reduce cobimetinib systemic exposure by more than 80%, significantly reducing its efficacy. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of colchicine by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as this interaction is considered serious. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of conivaptan by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as this interaction is considered serious. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as this interaction is considered serious. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of copanlisib by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers, as this may reduce copanlisib efficacy. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of cortisone by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as this interaction is considered serious. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of crizotinib by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Crizotinib increases rifampin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of cyclophosphamide by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of cyclosporine by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Pyrazinamide also decreases cyclosporine levels through an unknown mechanism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dabigatran by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as this interaction is considered serious. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dabrafenib by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as this interaction is considered serious. Danicopan increases the levels or effects of rifampin by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Consider dose reduction of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dantrolene by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of daprodustat by inducing CYP2C8 metabolism, potentially resulting in loss of efficacy. Monitor hemoglobin levels and adjust daprodustat dose when initiating or stopping therapy with CYP2C8 inducers. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dapsone by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of daridorexant by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as this interaction is considered serious. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of darifenacin by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as this interaction is considered serious. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of darolutamide by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with combined P-gp and strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated due to the potential for loss of therapeutic effect. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dasatinib by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as this interaction is considered serious. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of daunorubicin by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of deferasirox by inducing UGT metabolism. Avoid concomitant use with potent UGT inducers. If coadministration is required, consider increasing the initial dose of deferasirox and monitor ferritin levels and clinical response. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of deflazacort by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as this interaction is considered serious. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of deuruxolitinib by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as this interaction is considered serious. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dexamethasone by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as this interaction is considered serious. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of diazepam by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers may increase the rate of diazepam elimination, potentially reducing its efficacy. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of diclofenac by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of digoxin by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and increasing metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as this interaction is considered serious. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of diltiazem by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. If concomitant use is necessary, consider dosage adjustment and close monitoring of pharmacologic effects, such as blood pressure. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of disopyramide by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of docetaxel by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dolutegravir by increasing metabolism. Increase the dolutegravir dosage when coadministering with strong UGT1A/CYP3A4 inducers. Use an alternative to rifampin in patients with integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI)-associated resistance substitutions or suspected INSTI resistance, as concomitant use may result in loss of therapeutic effect and resistance development. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of donepezil by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of doravirine by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated due to the potential for loss of virologic response and resistance development. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of doxepin cream by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of doxorubicin by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of doxorubicin liposomal by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dronabinol by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dronedarone by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as this interaction is considered serious. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of duloxetine by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Coadministration is contraindicated. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dutasteride by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is necessary. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of duvelisib by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as this interaction is considered serious. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of edoxaban by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug, as this interaction is considered serious.
